newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Monday were bid $67.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $70.00, feedlot sources said.
Fed cattle prices this week were expected to trade $1.00 to $2.00 higher, supported by a strong tone to the beef market and moderate purchases last Friday by a large packer at $67.00, they said.
The activity by a large packer on a Friday, which is typically quiet, fueled ideas that beef demand was growing, the feedlot sources said.
"All things considered, this market could start at $68.00 and go higher, unless something unforeseen happens," one feedlot manager in the Texas Panhandle said.
Beef prices were seen rebounding this week amid ideas that packers were low on supplies and that retail demand for post-Easter promotions would continue strong, sources said.
Retail demand was expected to expand on ideas that steep price declines since March 4 had made beef attractive for advertising features, they said.
